note: Original hook templates written for HivemindOS. Categories are a conventional persuasion taxonomy; the five awareness levels are Eugene Schwartz's (Breakthrough Advertising, 1966). Pattern coverage was extended against the source credited in `credits`, with permission — the wording remains ours. These are authored patterns, not measured results: do not present them to a user as 'proven' or attach performance claims to them.

credits.permission: The author granted unrestricted use, including commercial use, in a direct message to the repository owner on 2026-07-10, in reply to an explicit question about commercial use and MIT licensing.

Two overlaps are inherent rather than borrowed: 'The Cold Open' (H087) is standard film vocabulary, and H077's repeated 'No more X.' scaffolding IS the pattern it names.

hooks.name: The Wrong Culprit
hooks.hook: There's a reason [OUTCOME] keeps happening, and it isn't [OBVIOUS CULPRIT].
hooks.whyItWorks: Names a symptom the viewer already feels, then denies the explanation they would have reached for, leaving a gap only you can close.
hooks.bestFor: Cold video where the audience feels the symptom but misdiagnoses it.
hooks.example: There's a reason your ads die on day three, and it isn't the algorithm.

hooks.name: The Metric That Mattered
hooks.hook: I tracked [METRIC] for [DURATION]. The number that mattered wasn't the one I was watching.
hooks.whyItWorks: Promises a payoff earned through visible effort, and implies the viewer is currently measuring the wrong thing.
hooks.bestFor: Data-led creators and analytics-heavy products.
hooks.example: I tracked my sleep for a year. The number that mattered wasn't hours.

hooks.name: The Unexplained Majority
hooks.hook: [NUMBER] of [GROUP] do this. Almost none of them can explain why it works.
hooks.whyItWorks: Social proof plus an unresolved mechanism — the viewer wants both the behavior and the explanation.
hooks.bestFor: Audiences who have heard the tactic but not the reasoning.
hooks.example: Nine of the top ten creators post at 6am. Almost none of them can explain why it works.

hooks.name: The Borrowed Field
hooks.hook: The most useful thing I learned about [TOPIC] came from [UNRELATED FIELD].
hooks.whyItWorks: An unexpected pairing defeats the viewer's prediction of where the video is going.
hooks.bestFor: Educational and thought-leadership content for cold audiences.
hooks.example: The most useful thing I learned about pricing came from emergency-room triage.

hooks.name: The Unfinished Cliche
hooks.hook: Stop me if you've heard this: [COMMON SETUP]. Here's the part nobody finishes.
hooks.whyItWorks: Acknowledges the audience's fatigue with the advice, then positions you as the one who completes it.
hooks.bestFor: Saturated niches where the surface advice is universally known.
hooks.example: Stop me if you've heard this: 'just post consistently.' Here's the part nobody finishes.

hooks.name: The Early Tell
hooks.hook: You can tell within [SHORT TIME] whether [THING] will work. Most people wait [LONG TIME].
hooks.whyItWorks: Offers a time saving and implies the viewer is currently wasting time, which stings enough to hold attention.
hooks.bestFor: Operators and practitioners who feel slow.
hooks.example: You can tell within 48 hours whether a creative will scale. Most people wait three weeks.

hooks.name: The Missing Hours
hooks.hook: [TASK] takes you [TIME]. It should take [SHORTER TIME]. Here's where the rest goes.
hooks.whyItWorks: Quantifies a loss the viewer has never actually added up, then promises to account for it.
hooks.bestFor: Efficiency and workflow tools.
hooks.example: Invoicing takes you six hours a month. It should take twenty minutes. Here's where the rest goes.

hooks.name: The Specific Moment
hooks.hook: If you've ever [SPECIFIC FRUSTRATING MOMENT], this is for you.
hooks.whyItWorks: Hyper-specific recognition beats a general problem statement — the viewer feels observed rather than marketed to.
hooks.bestFor: UGC and creator-led video.
hooks.example: If you've ever rewritten the same email four times before sending it, this is for you.

hooks.name: The Second-Order Pain
hooks.hook: The worst part of [PROBLEM] isn't [OBVIOUS PAIN]. It's [HIDDEN SECOND ORDER PAIN].
hooks.whyItWorks: Reframes a known problem so the viewer feels understood at a depth competitors have not reached.
hooks.bestFor: Considered purchases where the emotional cost outweighs the financial one.
hooks.example: The worst part of a failed launch isn't the lost revenue. It's not knowing which half to fix.

hooks.name: The Absolving Reframe
hooks.hook: You're not bad at [SKILL]. You're using a process built for [DIFFERENT SITUATION].
hooks.whyItWorks: Removes shame and relocates blame onto a system, which lowers defensiveness and buys attention.
hooks.bestFor: Audiences who have failed before and blame themselves.
hooks.example: You're not bad at hiring. You're using a process built for a company ten times your size.

hooks.name: The Shared Nightmare
hooks.hook: Every [ROLE] I talk to describes the same [COUNT]-step nightmare. Step [STEP] is where it breaks.
hooks.whyItWorks: Universalizes the pain (you are not alone) while isolating a single failure point (and it is fixable).
hooks.bestFor: B2B and professional audiences.
hooks.example: Every founder I talk to describes the same five-step nightmare. Step three is where it breaks.

hooks.name: The Running Total
hooks.hook: How much is [RECURRING PROBLEM] actually costing you? Do the math with me.
hooks.whyItWorks: An invitation to calculate is an invitation to participate, and the number always lands harder when the viewer derives it.
hooks.bestFor: High-ticket offers that need cost justification.
hooks.example: How much is your slowest onboarding step actually costing you? Do the math with me.

hooks.name: The Held Constant
hooks.hook: [BEFORE] to [AFTER] in [TIMEFRAME]. Same [CONSTRAINT], different [VARIABLE].
hooks.whyItWorks: Isolating one variable makes the result feel causal rather than lucky.
hooks.bestFor: Performance claims that need to survive skepticism.
hooks.example: From 1.2% to 4.8% conversion in six weeks. Same traffic, different first screen.

hooks.name: The Survivors
hooks.hook: We ran [NUMBER] [TESTS]. [SMALL NUMBER] beat the control. Here's what they shared.
hooks.whyItWorks: A low success rate is counterintuitively persuasive: it proves the test was real and the finding was earned.
hooks.bestFor: Data-driven brands and agencies.
hooks.example: We ran 140 landing pages. Six beat the control. Here's what they shared.

hooks.name: The Unprompted Chorus
hooks.hook: Don't take my word for it — here's [COUNT] [CUSTOMERS] describing the same result, unprompted.
hooks.whyItWorks: Repetition across independent voices reads as convergent evidence, not testimonial selection.
hooks.bestFor: Retargeting a product-aware audience.
hooks.example: Don't take my word for it — here's nine customers describing the same result, unprompted.

hooks.name: The Two Dates
hooks.hook: This is [THING] on [DATE]. This is the same [THING] on [LATER DATE].
hooks.whyItWorks: Time-stamped before-and-after removes the ambiguity that makes transformation claims feel staged.
hooks.bestFor: Visual results: fitness, design, restoration, dashboards.
hooks.example: This is the dashboard on March 3rd. This is the same dashboard on June 3rd.

hooks.name: The Refund Number
hooks.hook: [NUMBER] people bought [THING]. [NUMBER] asked for a refund. Here's why.
hooks.whyItWorks: Volunteering the negative number makes every other number credible.
hooks.bestFor: Products with strong retention and a skeptical market.
hooks.example: 3,400 people bought the course. 41 asked for a refund. Here's why.

hooks.name: The Raw Receipt
hooks.hook: I'll show you the raw [DATA], not the summary.
hooks.whyItWorks: Offering unpolished evidence signals you have nothing to hide, which is itself the proof.
hooks.bestFor: Markets numbed by curated case studies.
hooks.example: I'll show you the raw ad account, not the summary slide.

hooks.name: The Advice I Actually Give
hooks.hook: I've spent [DURATION] doing [THING] professionally. Here's the advice I actually give.
hooks.whyItWorks: The word 'actually' implies a public version and a private version, and promises the private one.
hooks.bestFor: Practitioner-led and expert content.
hooks.example: I've spent eleven years doing tax law professionally. Here's the advice I actually give.

hooks.name: The Stale Consensus
hooks.hook: [CREDENTIAL] here. The [INDUSTRY] consensus on [TOPIC] is out of date.
hooks.whyItWorks: Credential plus dissent — authority earns the hearing, disagreement earns the attention.
hooks.bestFor: Fields with a visible orthodoxy.
hooks.example: Structural engineer here. The consensus on timber high-rises is out of date.

hooks.name: The Early Signal
hooks.hook: After reviewing [COUNT] [ARTIFACTS], I can predict [OUTCOME] from [EARLY SIGNAL] alone.
hooks.whyItWorks: Volume establishes pattern-recognition authority; the narrow tell makes it feel like a learnable skill.
hooks.bestFor: Reviewers, judges, gatekeepers.
hooks.example: After reviewing 800 pitch decks, I can predict a pass from slide two alone.

hooks.name: The Insider Deviation
hooks.hook: The people who build [THING] don't use it the way you were taught.
hooks.whyItWorks: Implies a gap between public instruction and insider practice, and puts the viewer on the inside.
hooks.bestFor: Craft, tools, and technique content.
hooks.example: The people who build these knives don't sharpen them the way you were taught.

hooks.name: The Expensive Mistakes
hooks.hook: I've made every mistake in [DOMAIN]. These [COUNT] cost me the most.
hooks.whyItWorks: Authority through scar tissue rather than credentials, which is more transferable to a cold audience.
hooks.bestFor: Founder-led and creator-led brands.
hooks.example: I've made every mistake in ecommerce. These four cost me the most.

hooks.name: The Pre-Flight Checklist
hooks.hook: Here's the checklist I run before [HIGH STAKES ACTION].
hooks.whyItWorks: A checklist is a concrete, savable artifact, which drives both retention and shares.
hooks.bestFor: Content designed to be bookmarked.
hooks.example: Here's the checklist I run before every six-figure ad launch.

hooks.name: The Identical Work
hooks.hook: [APPROACH A] gets [MODEST RESULT]. [APPROACH B] gets [BETTER RESULT]. The work is identical.
hooks.whyItWorks: Equal effort with unequal outcome makes the change feel free, removing the main objection before it forms.
hooks.bestFor: Audiences already doing the work but getting nothing.
hooks.example: Posting daily gets you noise. Posting daily to one segment gets you customers. The work is identical.

hooks.name: The Split Test
hooks.hook: Same [INPUT]. Two [PROCESSES]. Watch what happens to [OUTPUT].
hooks.whyItWorks: A promised visual comparison creates a reason to stay for the reveal.
hooks.bestFor: Demonstrable, screen-recordable differences.
hooks.example: Same footage. Two edits. Watch what happens to watch time.

hooks.name: The Optimization Gap
hooks.hook: Beginners optimize [THING]. Professionals optimize [DIFFERENT THING].
hooks.whyItWorks: Nobody wants to be the beginner, so the viewer stays to check which one they are.
hooks.bestFor: Skill-progression and identity-adjacent content.
hooks.example: Beginners optimize the headline. Professionals optimize who sees it.

hooks.name: The Inverted Advice
hooks.hook: You were told to [CONVENTIONAL ADVICE]. Try the opposite for [SHORT PERIOD].
hooks.whyItWorks: A bounded experiment lowers the risk of trying, which makes a contrarian claim actionable instead of merely provocative.
hooks.bestFor: Audiences fatigued by standard advice.
hooks.example: You were told to niche down. Try the opposite for thirty days.

hooks.name: The Marketing Budget
hooks.hook: [EXPENSIVE OPTION] and [CHEAP OPTION] produce the same [RESULT]. Only one has a marketing budget.
hooks.whyItWorks: Positions you as the viewer's ally against an industry rather than as another seller inside it.
hooks.bestFor: Challenger brands undercutting an incumbent.
hooks.example: A $400 serum and a $12 one produce the same barrier repair. Only one has a marketing budget.

hooks.name: The Two Vocabularies
hooks.hook: What [GROUP A] calls [TERM] is what [GROUP B] calls [BLUNTER TERM].
hooks.whyItWorks: Translation between in-groups exposes a hidden cost and reads as candor.
hooks.bestFor: B2B and buyer-side audiences.
hooks.example: What agencies call 'brand awareness' is what your CFO calls 'unattributed spend.'

hooks.name: The Turn
hooks.hook: [TIME] ago I [LOW POINT]. Now I [CURRENT STATE]. The turn happened when [PIVOT].
hooks.whyItWorks: Names the pivot up front, so the viewer stays to learn the mechanism rather than the biography.
hooks.bestFor: Founder and creator origin content.
hooks.example: Two years ago I was invoicing $900 a month. Now it's $40k. The turn happened when I fired my biggest client.

hooks.name: The Message I Can't Forget
hooks.hook: A [CUSTOMER TYPE] sent me [ARTIFACT] last week. I haven't stopped thinking about it.
hooks.whyItWorks: Delegates the emotional claim to a third party, which lets you be moved rather than boastful.
hooks.bestFor: Mission-led brands and services.
hooks.example: A nurse sent me a photo of her fridge last week. I haven't stopped thinking about it.

hooks.name: The First Failure
hooks.hook: The first time I tried [THING], [SPECIFIC FAILURE]. Nobody warned me about [CAUSE].
hooks.whyItWorks: Vulnerability plus a named cause converts a story into a lesson the viewer can use.
hooks.bestFor: Educational content for people about to make the same mistake.
hooks.example: The first time I ran a webinar, four people showed up and three were my family. Nobody warned me about send-time decay.

hooks.name: The Question I Couldn't Answer
hooks.hook: My [RELATION] asked me why [PROBLEM]. I didn't have an answer. So I [ACTION].
hooks.whyItWorks: A personal stake explains why you did the work, which pre-empts the 'why should I trust you' objection.
hooks.bestFor: Investigative, mission, and category-creation stories.
hooks.example: My sister asked me why her insulin costs more than her rent. I didn't have an answer. So I spent a year finding one.

hooks.name: The Accidental Scope
hooks.hook: This started as [MODEST INTENT] and turned into [UNEXPECTED OUTCOME].
hooks.whyItWorks: Understated origin makes the outcome feel discovered rather than engineered, which disarms sales resistance.
hooks.bestFor: Products with a genuine scratch-your-own-itch origin.
hooks.example: This started as a spreadsheet for my own bookkeeping and turned into a product 6,000 people pay for.

hooks.name: The Near Quit
hooks.hook: I almost quit [PURSUIT] over [INCIDENT]. Here's what changed my mind.
hooks.whyItWorks: Stakes are established in one sentence, and the resolution is withheld.
hooks.bestFor: Long-form and serialized creator content.
hooks.example: I almost quit woodworking over a single warped tabletop. Here's what changed my mind.

hooks.name: The Dated Change
hooks.hook: [CHANGE] takes effect [DATE]. If you [ACTION] before then, [BENEFIT].
hooks.whyItWorks: Urgency sourced from an external, verifiable event rather than an invented countdown.
hooks.bestFor: Regulatory, pricing, and seasonal deadlines.
hooks.example: The new import duty takes effect January 1st. If you order before then, you pay the old rate.

hooks.name: The Meter
hooks.hook: Every [TIME UNIT] you wait costs [QUANTIFIED LOSS].
hooks.whyItWorks: Converts inaction from a neutral default into an ongoing, quantified expense.
hooks.bestFor: Finance, health, and compounding-benefit offers.
hooks.example: Every month you wait costs about $2,300 in compounding interest.

hooks.name: The Honest Cap
hooks.hook: [COUNT] spots. [COUNT] taken. I close it when it's full, not when a timer runs out.
hooks.whyItWorks: Explicitly rejecting the fake-deadline tactic makes the real constraint believable.
hooks.bestFor: Services and cohorts with genuine capacity limits.
hooks.example: Twelve spots. Nine taken. I close it when it's full, not when a timer runs out.

hooks.name: The Closing Window
hooks.hook: This works right now because [TEMPORARY CONDITION]. That condition is closing.
hooks.whyItWorks: Urgency attached to an opportunity rather than to an offer, which survives a skeptical audience.
hooks.bestFor: Platform arbitrage and early-mover plays.
hooks.example: This works right now because the platform still favors long captions. That condition is closing.

hooks.name: The Second-Best Time
hooks.hook: The best time to [ACTION] was [PAST]. The second best is before [NEAR EVENT].
hooks.whyItWorks: Acknowledges the viewer's regret, then immediately gives them a way out of it.
hooks.bestFor: Long-horizon decisions the viewer has been deferring.
hooks.example: The best time to start was five years ago. The second best is before the rate cut.

hooks.name: The Stated Constraint
hooks.hook: I'm taking this down [WHEN] — not as a tactic. [GENUINE REASON].
hooks.whyItWorks: Naming the tactic you are not using is the only way to use a deadline on an audience that has seen every deadline.
hooks.bestFor: Warm lists that have been sold to before.
hooks.example: I'm taking this down Friday — not as a tactic. I can't support more than thirty people at once.

hooks.name: The Stop
hooks.hook: Don't [EXPECTED ACTION]. Put it down.
hooks.whyItWorks: A direct command interrupts scroll momentum because it demands compliance before comprehension.
hooks.bestFor: First-frame attention capture on cold feeds.
hooks.example: Don't buy the protein powder. Put it down.

hooks.name: The Wrong-Sounding Truth
hooks.hook: This is going to sound wrong: [COUNTERINTUITIVE STATEMENT].
hooks.whyItWorks: Pre-labeling the claim as counterintuitive buys you the two seconds needed to justify it.
hooks.bestFor: Contrarian positioning that still needs to land as credible.
hooks.example: This is going to sound wrong: raising your price is the fastest way to get more customers.

hooks.name: The Interrupt
hooks.hook: [ABRUPT PHYSICAL ACTION]. Now that I have your attention — [PAYLOAD].
hooks.whyItWorks: A physical pattern break resets visual attention, and naming it prevents the gimmick from feeling cheap.
hooks.bestFor: High-scroll-velocity placements.
hooks.example: (Drops the mug.) Now that I have your attention — that mug cost less than your monthly software bill.

hooks.name: The Retraction
hooks.hook: Wrong. [COMMON CLAIM] is wrong, and I used to teach it.
hooks.whyItWorks: Self-implication converts a contrarian take from an attack into a confession, which is far harder to dismiss.
hooks.bestFor: Educators correcting their own field.
hooks.example: Wrong. 'Hook them in three seconds' is wrong, and I used to teach it.

hooks.name: The Self-Aware Skip
hooks.hook: Skip the first [COUNT] seconds of every video like this one. Including this one. Except—
hooks.whyItWorks: Meta-awareness of the format earns goodwill from an audience that resents being hooked.
hooks.bestFor: Sophisticated, ad-literate audiences.
hooks.example: Skip the first five seconds of every video like this one. Including this one. Except I already started.

hooks.name: The Bare Take
hooks.hook: No hook. No music. Just [COUNT] seconds on [TOPIC].
hooks.whyItWorks: Refusing production signals that the content can carry itself, which is a production choice that reads as none.
hooks.bestFor: Expertise-led content in overproduced niches.
hooks.example: No hook. No music. Just forty seconds on why your retention drops at 0:07.

hooks.name: The Tell
hooks.hook: If you [SPECIFIC BEHAVIOR], you already think like [IDENTITY].
hooks.whyItWorks: Flatters the viewer with an identity they have not claimed yet, using evidence they recognize in themselves.
hooks.bestFor: Community building and category entry.
hooks.example: If you reread your own sent emails, you already think like an editor.

hooks.name: The Precise Segment
hooks.hook: This isn't for everyone. It's for [SEGMENT] who [CONDITION].
hooks.whyItWorks: Exclusion is a qualification device: the people who stay are the ones worth reaching.
hooks.bestFor: High-ticket and narrow-fit offers.
hooks.example: This isn't for everyone. It's for solo consultants who've stopped taking on hourly work.

hooks.name: The Two Kinds
hooks.hook: There are two kinds of [ROLE]. The difference shows up in [OBSERVABLE BEHAVIOR].
hooks.whyItWorks: Forces self-classification, and self-classification requires watching to the end.
hooks.bestFor: Professional and craft audiences.
hooks.example: There are two kinds of engineers. The difference shows up in how they name variables at 2am.

hooks.name: The Underlying Want
hooks.hook: You don't want [SURFACE WANT]. You want [UNDERLYING WANT].
hooks.whyItWorks: Reframing the goal repositions your product against the real motivation rather than its proxy.
hooks.bestFor: Categories where the stated goal is a vanity metric.
hooks.example: You don't want more followers. You want to stop explaining what you do at parties.

hooks.name: The Reframe
hooks.hook: [GROUP] have been told they're [NEGATIVE LABEL]. They're [REFRAME].
hooks.whyItWorks: Defends a group against a label they have internalized, which buys loyalty before it asks for anything.
hooks.bestFor: Audiences with a shared, unfair reputation.
hooks.example: Career switchers have been told they're behind. They're compounding two curves at once.

hooks.name: The Self-Selecting Sentence
hooks.hook: The [COUNT] people this is for will know by the end of this sentence.
hooks.whyItWorks: Extreme narrowing signals confidence and filters the audience down to buyers.
hooks.bestFor: Warm lists and niche launches.
hooks.example: The four people this is for will know by the end of this sentence.

hooks.name: The Named Parts
hooks.hook: [RESULT] isn't luck. It's [NAMED MECHANISM], and it has [COUNT] parts.
hooks.whyItWorks: Naming a mechanism converts a mystery into a system, and a system implies it can be taught.
hooks.bestFor: Frameworks, courses, and methodology-led offers.
hooks.example: Virality isn't luck. It's forwardable tension, and it has three parts.

hooks.name: The Live Explanation
hooks.hook: Here's what's actually happening when [OBSERVABLE EVENT].
hooks.whyItWorks: Explains something the viewer has seen many times but never understood, which is inherently satisfying.
hooks.bestFor: Science, craft, and how-things-work content.
hooks.example: Here's what's actually happening when your sourdough collapses in the oven.

hooks.name: The Symmetric Failure
hooks.hook: [THING] works because of [MECHANISM] — which is also why it fails at [EDGE CASE].
hooks.whyItWorks: Explaining the failure mode with the same mechanism proves you understand it rather than repeating it.
hooks.bestFor: Sophisticated audiences that have already tried the thing.
hooks.example: Cold plunges work because of hormetic stress — which is also why they fail if you do them right after lifting.

hooks.name: The Single Moving Part
hooks.hook: [THING] has one moving part. Once you see it, you can't unsee it.
hooks.whyItWorks: Promises a permanent perceptual upgrade for a very small time investment.
hooks.bestFor: Analysis and teardown formats.
hooks.example: Every pricing page has one moving part. Once you see it, you can't unsee it.

hooks.name: The Root, Not the Symptom
hooks.hook: Most [SOLUTIONS] treat [SYMPTOM]. This one changes [ROOT CAUSE].
hooks.whyItWorks: Reclassifies every competitor as superficial without naming or attacking any of them.
hooks.bestFor: Differentiation against a crowded field.
hooks.example: Most acne treatments treat the spot. This one changes the oil that feeds it.

hooks.name: The Teachable Minute
hooks.hook: Give me [SHORT TIME] and you'll understand [TOPIC] well enough to explain it.
hooks.whyItWorks: The promise is not knowledge but status — being the person at the table who can explain it.
hooks.bestFor: Explainer content on intimidating topics.
hooks.example: Give me ninety seconds and you'll understand inflation well enough to explain it at dinner.

hooks.name: The Public Wrong
hooks.hook: I was wrong about [BELIEF]. Publicly. For [DURATION].
hooks.whyItWorks: Admitting a durable, public error is expensive, and expense is what makes the correction credible.
hooks.bestFor: Established voices with a record to revise.
hooks.example: I was wrong about remote work. Publicly. For four years.

hooks.name: The Skipped Practice
hooks.hook: I don't do [WIDELY RECOMMENDED PRACTICE], and my [METRIC] is fine.
hooks.whyItWorks: Contradicts a rule the viewer feels guilty about breaking, which is an immediate relief and an immediate question.
hooks.bestFor: Audiences drowning in best practices.
hooks.example: I don't post daily, and my revenue is fine.

hooks.name: The Part That Doesn't Work
hooks.hook: Here's the part of [MY THING] that doesn't work yet.
hooks.whyItWorks: Volunteering a weakness pre-empts the objection and makes the strengths audible.
hooks.bestFor: Product-aware audiences comparing options.
hooks.example: Here's the part of our onboarding that doesn't work yet.

hooks.name: The Long Embarrassment
hooks.hook: I've been [DOING THING] for [DURATION] and I still [ADMISSION].
hooks.whyItWorks: Expertise plus fallibility is more relatable than expertise alone, and it lowers the barrier to trying.
hooks.bestFor: Skill content aimed at intimidated beginners.
hooks.example: I've been cooking professionally for twelve years and I still burn garlic.

hooks.name: The Uncomfortable Price
hooks.hook: We raised the price and I felt sick about it. Here's the reasoning.
hooks.whyItWorks: Narrating the discomfort of a commercial decision makes the decision feel honest rather than extractive.
hooks.bestFor: Warm audiences reacting to a pricing change.
hooks.example: We raised the price 40% and I felt sick about it. Here's the reasoning.

hooks.name: The Owed Update
hooks.hook: Nobody asked, but I owe you an update on [PAST CLAIM].
hooks.whyItWorks: Voluntary accountability to a promise nobody was tracking is the cheapest trust you will ever buy.
hooks.bestFor: Serialized content and long-term audiences.
hooks.example: Nobody asked, but I owe you an update on the 90-day challenge I promised in March.

hooks.name: The Narrow Truth
hooks.hook: [BELIEF] is true for [NARROW CASE]. For everyone else it's actively harmful.
hooks.whyItWorks: Concedes the rule before overturning it, which is harder to argue with than a flat contradiction.
hooks.bestFor: Advice that has escaped its original context.
hooks.example: 'Fail fast' is true for seed-stage software. For everyone else it's actively harmful.

hooks.name: The Unnecessary Requirement
hooks.hook: You do not need [ASSUMED REQUIREMENT] to [OUTCOME]. I'll prove it.
hooks.whyItWorks: Removes the barrier the viewer believes is disqualifying them, then stakes your credibility on proving it.
hooks.bestFor: Audiences who think they are not eligible yet.
hooks.example: You do not need a following to make your first $10k. I'll prove it.

hooks.name: The Different Problem
hooks.hook: [SOURCE] popularized [ADVICE]. They were solving a different problem.
hooks.whyItWorks: Attacks the provenance of the advice rather than the advice itself, which is both fairer and more devastating.
hooks.bestFor: Industries running on cargo-culted practice.
hooks.example: Google popularized the coding interview. They were solving a different problem.

hooks.name: The Bad Statistic
hooks.hook: The [STATISTIC EVERYONE QUOTES] comes from [FLAWED ORIGIN]. Look it up.
hooks.whyItWorks: An invitation to verify is a confidence display, and the viewer almost never takes it.
hooks.bestFor: Niches with one famous, load-bearing statistic.
hooks.example: The '8-second attention span' stat comes from a study that never existed. Look it up.

hooks.name: The Expensive Sentence
hooks.hook: '[COMMON PHRASE]' is the most expensive sentence in [INDUSTRY].
hooks.whyItWorks: Attaches a cost to a phrase the viewer has said out loud, making the pain personal and specific.
hooks.bestFor: Insider audiences who know the phrase.
hooks.example: 'We'll fix it in post' is the most expensive sentence in film.

hooks.name: The Outdated Assumption
hooks.hook: Everything you were taught about [TOPIC] assumes [OUTDATED CONDITION].
hooks.whyItWorks: Invalidates a whole body of advice in one clause, which is a larger promise than correcting a single point.
hooks.bestFor: Categories reshaped by a recent structural change.
hooks.example: Everything you were taught about saving assumes 5% interest.

hooks.name: The Shock Stat
hooks.hook: [SURPRISING STATISTIC]. And it's about to matter for your [RELEVANT THING].
hooks.whyItWorks: A precise, unexpected number is treated as evidence before it is examined, which buys the second sentence.
hooks.bestFor: Health, finance, and other data-heavy categories.
hooks.example: Two-thirds of first-time founders never take a salary. And it's about to matter for your runway.

hooks.name: The Quiz
hooks.hook: Which of these two [OPTIONS] actually [OUTCOME]? Most people pick wrong.
hooks.whyItWorks: A question the viewer silently answers is a commitment; they stay to learn whether they were right.
hooks.bestFor: Comparison content and myth correction.
hooks.example: Which of these two labels actually means the eggs were pasture-raised? Most people pick wrong.

hooks.name: The Failed Attempts
hooks.hook: Tried [FIRST FIX]. Tried [SECOND FIX]. Tried [THIRD FIX]. Nothing held. Then [TURN].
hooks.whyItWorks: Enumerating the viewer's own failed attempts proves you have stood where they stand, before you offer anything.
hooks.bestFor: Audiences who already bought a competitor and were disappointed.
hooks.example: Tried melatonin. Tried blackout curtains. Tried cutting caffeine. Nothing held. Then I moved dinner two hours earlier.

hooks.name: The Normalized Problem
hooks.hook: You think [COMMON EXPERIENCE] is normal. It isn't, and [CONSEQUENCE].
hooks.whyItWorks: Reclassifying a tolerated condition as a problem manufactures the demand the rest of the video serves.
hooks.bestFor: Categories where the suffering is quietly accepted as the cost of living.
hooks.example: You think being useless at 3pm every day is normal. It isn't, and it's eating your best two hours.

hooks.name: The Enumerated Relief
hooks.hook: No more [FIRST PAIN]. No more [SECOND PAIN]. No more [THIRD PAIN]. Just [RESULT].
hooks.whyItWorks: Anaphora stacks the pains into a rhythm, then discharges all of them in a single clause.
hooks.bestFor: Products that resolve several frustrations rather than one.
hooks.example: No more spreadsheets. No more chasing receipts. No more March panic. Just a number you can trust.

hooks.name: The Named Quote
hooks.hook: "[VERBATIM CUSTOMER SENTENCE]" — [NAME], [ROLE OR CREDENTIAL].
hooks.whyItWorks: One attributed sentence carrying a specific, un-marketable detail outperforms a wall of anonymous praise.
hooks.bestFor: Product-aware audiences who need one believable voice rather than many.
hooks.example: "I stopped rebuilding the invoice template every single month." — Dana R., freelance illustrator.

hooks.name: The Converted Skeptic
hooks.hook: I thought [THING] was [DISMISSAL]. Then [SPECIFIC RESULT].
hooks.whyItWorks: Voicing the audience's objection yourself means the rebuttal arrives on their side of the argument.
hooks.bestFor: Categories carrying a credibility problem.
hooks.example: I thought cold email was dead. Then a two-line message booked eleven calls in a week.

hooks.name: The Third-Party Verdict
hooks.hook: [INDEPENDENT EXPERT] looked at [THING] and said [SHORT VERDICT].
hooks.whyItWorks: Borrowed authority from someone with no stake in the sale is the cheapest credibility available.
hooks.bestFor: Technical products the audience cannot evaluate for themselves.
hooks.example: A dermatologist read the ingredient list and said only one line on it mattered.

hooks.name: The Vindication
hooks.hook: They laughed when I [UNCONVENTIONAL ACTION]. Then [RESULT].
hooks.whyItWorks: Social risk followed by payoff is the oldest narrative shape there is, and it survives any level of ad literacy.
hooks.bestFor: Founder stories and contrarian bets.
hooks.example: They laughed when I deleted every social account. Then revenue doubled.

hooks.name: The Proxy Test
hooks.hook: I tried [THING] for [DURATION] so you don't have to. The verdict:
hooks.whyItWorks: Positions you as having already paid the cost the viewer would pay, which makes it a gift before it is a pitch.
hooks.bestFor: Review, comparison, and trend content.
hooks.example: I tried every AI note-taker for thirty days so you don't have to. The verdict:

hooks.name: The Day in the Life
hooks.hook: A day of [ROLE] work, start to finish — and the [MOMENT] where [THING] earns its keep.
hooks.whyItWorks: Format-driven rather than sentence-driven: the promise is access, and the product arrives as a consequence rather than a claim.
hooks.bestFor: Organic-feeling creator content and native placements.
hooks.example: A day of freelance editing, start to finish — and the twenty minutes where the transcript tool earns its keep.

hooks.name: The Day After
hooks.hook: Here's what [ORDINARY MOMENT] looks like once [PAIN] is behind you.
hooks.whyItWorks: Future-pacing lets the viewer occupy the outcome before they have paid for it.
hooks.bestFor: Transformation offers whose after-state is emotional rather than numeric.
hooks.example: Here's what Sunday evening looks like once the job you dread is behind you.

hooks.name: The Release
hooks.hook: You've researched enough. [ACTION].
hooks.whyItWorks: Some audiences are not missing information; they are waiting to be released. Saying so is the entire hook.
hooks.bestFor: Warm lists that have consumed everything and bought nothing.
hooks.example: You've researched enough. Book the consult.

hooks.name: The Hard Word
hooks.hook: Nobody is going to say this to you kindly, so: [HARD TRUTH]. And [CONSEQUENCE] is already happening.
hooks.whyItWorks: Direct confrontation, used sparingly, cuts through an audience anaesthetised by encouragement.
hooks.bestFor: Audiences the category has coddled. Overuse reads as contempt.
hooks.example: Nobody is going to say this to you kindly, so: your rate hasn't moved in four years. And inflation already took the raise.

hooks.name: The Cold Open
hooks.hook: [OPEN MID ACTION WITH NO CONTEXT]
hooks.whyItWorks: Withholding all setup makes the viewer stay to work out what they walked into. The hook is the absence of one.
hooks.bestFor: Feeds where every competing video opens by announcing itself.
hooks.example: (Camera starts mid-sentence, hands already inside a dismantled engine.) — and that's the part nobody ever replaces.

hooks.name: The POV
hooks.hook: POV: you're [ORDINARY SCENARIO] and [UNEXPECTED THING] happens.
hooks.whyItWorks: Second-person framing conscripts the viewer into the scene rather than describing it to them.
hooks.bestFor: Short-form native formats where the convention is already established.
hooks.example: POV: you're on hold with your bank and the agent already knows why you called.

hooks.name: The Effort Removal
hooks.hook: You don't need [PAINFUL REQUIREMENT]. You need [ACTUAL MECHANISM].
hooks.whyItWorks: Every audience is braced for more work. Removing the requirement is a larger promise than improving the result.
hooks.bestFor: Categories that sell discipline, hustle, or sheer volume.
hooks.example: You don't need more willpower. You need to stop keeping the snacks in the house.

hooks.name: The Forbidden Post
hooks.hook: I was told not to post this. [REVEAL].
hooks.whyItWorks: Implied risk to the speaker makes the content feel unsanctioned, and therefore true.
hooks.bestFor: Genuine insider content. Use only when the risk is real, or it reads as theatre.
hooks.example: I was told not to post this. Here's what the supplier actually charges us.

hooks.name: The Sooner
hooks.hook: What I wish someone had told me [TIMEFRAME] ago about [TOPIC].
hooks.whyItWorks: Regret is a gift-wrapped lesson: the speaker has already paid for it and is handing it over.
hooks.bestFor: Mentorship and education content.
hooks.example: What I wish someone had told me five years ago about pricing my own work.

hooks.name: The Incentive
hooks.hook: [GROUP] won't tell you [TRUTH]. It would cost them [WHAT THEY LOSE].
hooks.whyItWorks: Explaining the economic reason for a silence is far more persuasive than alleging a conspiracy behind it.
hooks.bestFor: Categories with a visible, conflicted intermediary.
hooks.example: Dealerships won't tell you the financing is where the margin lives. It would cost them the margin.
